originalTitle: Editor of top Ethiopian independent news site seized by police, publisher says
title: Who Tells Our Stories? News from Ethiopia
content:
Hello, News Explorers!

Hello, hello, amazing news explorers! It's your kid-friendly news reporter here, bringing you stories from our wonderful continent, Africa! Africa is so big and beautiful, full of different countries, amazing animals, and incredible people. Today, we're going on a special journey to a country called Ethiopia. Have you heard of Ethiopia? It's a place with ancient history, delicious food, and friendly smiles.

What is News?

Do you ever wonder what's happening in your town, or in another country far away? That's what news is for! News tells us what is happening in the world. It's like a big window that shows us new things every day. News can tell us about a new school opening, a big football game, or even about someone helping others. Knowing the news helps us learn and understand our world better. It helps us know about good things and sometimes, not-so-good things too. Did you know? The very first newspapers were like big letters written by hand and shared in ancient Rome! Imagine someone writing a newspaper for you by hand!

Meet the News Heroes: Reporters and Editors

To get the news, we have special people called reporters. Reporters are like super detectives! They go out, they listen, they ask questions, and they find out what's happening. They talk to many people to get all sides of a story. Then, they write down everything they learned. But before the news reaches your ears or eyes, there's another hero: the editor! An editor is like a captain of a ship. They read all the stories from the reporters. They check if the stories are clear, true, and fair. They make sure everything makes sense and is easy to understand. They are very important because they help make sure we get the best and truest news possible.

Independent News – Telling All Sides

Now, there are different kinds of news. Some news comes from places that are run by the government. Other news comes from places that are "independent." What does "independent" mean? It means they are free! They are not told what to say by the government or by anyone else who might want to hide something. Independent news sites try their best to tell stories just as they are, even if those stories are tricky or make some powerful people unhappy. They believe it's important for everyone to know the full truth, so they can make up their own minds. They want to share all parts of a story, not just one part. Did you know? Ethiopia is sometimes called the "cradle of humanity" because some of the oldest human fossils were found there! That means it's a very old and special place.

A Story from Ethiopia: Our Story-Teller Friend

Recently, something happened in Ethiopia that we want to tell you about. There was an editor, a very important story-checker, from an independent news site. We'll call him our "story-teller friend." His job was to make sure the news shared on his site was true and fair. But one day, the police came and took him away. His news company, his publisher, said he was taken. The police are people who work to keep everyone safe and follow the rules. They wear special uniforms and help keep order in our communities. But when a story-teller friend is taken, especially from a news place that tries to tell all sides, it makes people wonder why. It makes us think about what happened and if everything is okay.

What are Rights Groups?

When something like this happens, there are special groups of people who speak up. They are called "rights groups." Think of them as super-helpers for everyone's rights. What are "rights"? Rights are like rules that say how everyone should be treated fairly. For example, you have a right to learn and play. Adults have rights too, like the right to speak their mind and share information, as long as it's truthful. These rights groups said that taking our story-teller friend is part of a "pattern." A pattern means it's happened before, not just once. They are worried that other news places might also be stopped from sharing stories. They want to make sure everyone's rights are protected. Did you know? The Ethiopian calendar is different from many other calendars! It's usually 7 or 8 years behind the calendar most people use. So if it's 2024 for you, it might be 2016 or 2017 in Ethiopia!

Why is this Important? Speaking Up and Listening

Why does this matter, especially for you, young news explorers? Because it's important for everyone to be able to speak their mind and share what they know. This is called "freedom of speech" or "freedom of the press" for news people. Imagine if you had a super exciting story to tell your friends, but someone told you, "No, you can't tell that story!" How would that make you feel? Not very happy, right? You would feel like your voice isn't being heard. When news people can't share stories freely, it means we might not know everything that's happening. It's like having only one side of a conversation, and we miss out on hearing other voices. We need all voices to understand the world fully and make good decisions.

What Happens Next?

Right now, the government, the people in charge of Ethiopia, has not said anything about why our story-teller friend was taken. When someone doesn't say anything, it can make people even more curious and worried. We all want to understand. We hope that soon, everyone will understand why this happened and that our story-teller friend will be able to go back to his important job of sharing news. His work helps many people learn and understand.

Let's Be Curious!

So, young news explorers, remember how important news is! It helps us learn, grow, and understand. Always be curious, always ask questions, and always try to learn from many different places. That way, you'll grow up to be smart and understand our big, beautiful world even better! Keep exploring and keep learning!
summary: An editor from an independent news site in Ethiopia, who helps share stories, was taken by police, which has made groups who protect people's rights very worried about everyone's freedom to share information.
whyMatters: This is important because it reminds us that everyone, including kids, needs truthful stories to understand the world, and when news people can't share stories freely, we might miss out on important information and different ideas.

originalTitle: Does Africa still back Infantino as Fifa president?
title: Who Leads Our Big Football Family? Africa's Choice!
content:
Hello, My Football Friends!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly reporter, Zola, here from Africa! I love football, and I bet you do too! It's super fun to watch, play, and cheer for our favourite teams. Today, we're going to talk about someone very important in the world of football. He's like the biggest boss for football all over the planet! His name is Mr. Gianni Infantino. He leads a very big group called FIFA. FIFA helps make sure football is fair and fun for everyone, everywhere. Let's learn about him and what our African football family thinks! It's an exciting time for football across our amazing continent.

What is FIFA?

First, let's talk about FIFA. FIFA is like the world's biggest club for football. It's not just for one country, but for almost every country! It helps set the rules for games, organises big tournaments like the World Cup, and helps countries grow their football. Think of it like a big helper for all our football dreams. FIFA wants more kids like you to play football and have wonderful fields to play on. They also help coaches learn new things so our players can become super stars! Did you know? FIFA has more countries as members than the United Nations! That's how many countries love football!

Who is Mr. Gianni Infantino?

Mr. Gianni Infantino is the big boss of FIFA. He is called the President. Imagine being the president of all football in the whole wide world! That's his job. He helps make big decisions about football. He travels around to different countries, talks to football leaders, and tries to make football even better for everyone. He's been the president for some years now. He loves football, just like us! His job is super important because he helps make sure our favourite game keeps growing and makes people happy. He often talks about making football truly global, meaning he wants every part of the world, including Africa, to have amazing football.

Why is Mr. Infantino Important for Africa?

So, why does Mr. Infantino and FIFA matter to us here in Africa? Well, FIFA helps African football a lot! They give money to build new football fields and training centres. This means more places for kids like you to play and learn. They also help our coaches get better training. This makes our players stronger and smarter on the field. FIFA also helps make sure our African teams can play in big tournaments, like the World Cup! They want African football to be strong and shine brightly for everyone to see. Mr. Infantino often visits African countries to meet our football leaders and see how FIFA can help more. He promises to keep helping our football grow and make it world-class. He knows how much passion we have for the game here. Did you know? FIFA has a special programme called 'Forward' that gives money to football associations all over the world, including many in Africa, to develop football! This money helps build stadiums and train young players.

What Does "Backing" Mean?

Now, let's talk about a big word: 'backing.' When we say, 'Does Africa still back Mr. Infantino?', it just means, 'Do our African football leaders want him to continue being the big boss of FIFA?' It means, 'Do they support him to keep doing his job?' Just like when you back your friend in a game, you want them to do well and keep playing. Our African football leaders need to decide if they think Mr. Infantino is doing a good job for Africa and if they want him to keep leading FIFA for another time. It's a big decision for them. They think very carefully about it.

What Are African Leaders Thinking?

Our African football leaders are very important people. They lead the football in our own countries. They are thinking about this big decision. The news says that our African football family has not said 'yes' or 'no' officially yet. This means they are still talking and thinking very hard. They want to make the best choice for all of African football. They might be looking at all the things Mr. Infantino has done and what he promises to do next. Some leaders might feel happy with his work, and some might want to see more good things happen before they decide. It's like when you are choosing which flavour of ice cream to pick – you think about all the yummy options before you make up your mind! They are having important meetings to talk about what is best for the future of our game across the continent.

Why Is This Decision Important?

This decision is very important for African football. If our African leaders decide to back Mr. Infantino, it means they believe he will keep helping our football grow and become even better. It means more support for our young players, better facilities, and more chances for our teams to shine on the world stage. If they don't back him, it might mean they want someone else to lead FIFA, someone they think might help Africa even more. But for now, they are still talking and listening to each other. They want to make a choice that will bring more joy and success to football across our whole continent. Their decision will affect how much money comes to Africa for football, how many World Cup spots we get, and how we develop new talents. It's all about making African football stronger and more visible around the world. Did you know? Africa has 54 different countries that are part of FIFA! That's a lot of countries working together for football!

What Happens Next?

Soon, our football leaders will finish their discussions. They will talk to each other and then make a choice. We will hear what they decide. Whatever happens, one thing is for sure: football in Africa will keep growing! We have so much talent, so much passion, and so many young dreams. The leaders are working hard to make sure those dreams can come true. We will keep playing, cheering, and loving our beautiful game! Their main goal is to ensure that football continues to bring happiness and opportunities to all Africans.

Let's Keep Loving Football!

So, my friends, while the grown-ups are making big decisions, let's keep playing football! Let's keep supporting our teams! And let's remember that football brings us all together, no matter where we are in Africa. It teaches us teamwork, fair play, and how to have lots of fun. Thank you for listening! This is Zola, your kid-friendly reporter, signing off! See you on the pitch!
summary: African football leaders are thinking about whether to support Mr. Gianni Infantino to keep his job as the big boss of FIFA, the world's football organisation, because his decisions help African football grow.
whyMatters: This is important because the person who leads FIFA makes big choices that help our African football grow, build fields, and send our teams to big games, bringing joy to many kids like you!
